name: Uzbek
catalog_quote: Stress is phonemic both on the word level and in longer utterances (i.e. the position of the various stresses can be significant for meaning). The stress patterns on the sentence level, however, are highly variable.

Proceedings of the Workshop on Turkic and Languages in Contact with Turkic 5: 1-15. doi:10.3765/ptu.v5i1.4796 (CC BY 4.0; downloaded via Internet Archive copy of the LSA PDF, live site could not be reached by automated download)

sources.quote: p.2: 'Like Turkish, Uzbek is reported to have final lexical stress ... (from Sjoberg 1963: 24-5) [ortoq] friend, [ortoq-lar] friends, [ortoq-lar-i], [ortoq-lar-i-ga] ... Also like Turkish, Uzbek is reported to have, in addition to its canonical final stress, cases in which stress appears in other positions within a word ... lexical exceptions, including loanwords, function words, and proper names ... certain affixes that may require stress to be placed prior to the final syllable (pre-stressing negation -ma, equative -daj/-daqa, personal copula particles).' p.13 Conclusions: in the Non-Focus c
